title: 110. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Comparing Ratios with Different Units
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Length Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two length ratios by converting both to the same unit.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(3\text{ m}:80\text{ cm}\) or \(2\text{ m}:50\text{ cm}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert both ratios to centimetres. For \(3\text{ m}:80\text{ cm}\), \(3\text{ m}=300\text{ cm}\), so the ratio is \(300:80=15:4=3.75\). For \(2\text{ m}:50\text{ cm}\), \(2\text{ m}=200\text{ cm}\), so the ratio is \(200:50=4:1=4\). Since \(4>3.75\), the ratio \(2\text{ m}:50\text{ cm}\) is greater.
questions.hint: Convert corresponding quantities to a common unit before comparing.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Time Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two time ratios by converting hours to minutes.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(30\text{ min}:2\text{ h}\) or \(20\text{ min}:1.5\text{ h}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert hours to minutes. \(30\text{ min}:2\text{ h}=30:120=1:4=0.25\). \(20\text{ min}:1.5\text{ h}=20:90=2:9\approx 0.222\). Since \(0.25>0.222\), the ratio \(30\text{ min}:2\text{ h}\) is greater.
questions.hint: Express each ratio in the same units and in the same order.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Mass Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two mass ratios by converting kilograms to grams.
questions.question: Which statement is correct for the ratios \(500\text{ g}:2\text{ kg}\) and \(300\text{ g}:1.2\text{ kg}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert kilograms to grams. \(500\text{ g}:2\text{ kg}=500:2{,}000=1:4=0.25\). \(300\text{ g}:1.2\text{ kg}=300:1{,}200=1:4=0.25\). Since both simplify to the same value, the two ratios are equal.
questions.hint: Find the two unit rates before deciding which is greater.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Time Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two distance-time ratios by converting to the same time unit.
questions.question: Which statement is correct for \(60\text{ km}:45\text{ min}\) and \(80\text{ km}:1\text{ h}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert the first time to hours: \(45\text{ min}=0.75\text{ h}\). The numerical rates in kilometres per hour are \(\frac{60}{0.75}=80\) and \(\frac{80}{1}=80\). Both ratios therefore represent \(80\text{ km/h}\), so they are equal; the first ratio is not greater.
questions.hint: Convert corresponding quantities to a common unit before comparing.

questions.concept: Comparing Unit Prices with Different Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two cost-to-mass ratios by converting to the same mass unit.
questions.question: Which is the greater unit price, \(12\text{ yuan}:500\text{ g}\) or \(20\text{ yuan}:1\text{ kg}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert \(500\text{ g}=0.5\text{ kg}\). In yuan per kilogram, the numerical unit prices are \(\frac{12}{0.5}=24\) and \(\frac{20}{1}=20\), giving \(24\text{ yuan/kg}\) and \(20\text{ yuan/kg}\). Since \(24>20\), the first unit price is greater; the alternative selects the smaller unit price.
questions.hint: Express each ratio in the same units and in the same order.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Volume Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two volume ratios by converting litres to millilitres.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(1.5\text{ L}:250\text{ mL}\) or \(2\text{ L}:400\text{ mL}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert litres to millilitres. \(1.5\text{ L}:250\text{ mL}=1{,}500:250=6\). \(2\text{ L}:400\text{ mL}=2{,}000:400=5\). Since \(6>5\), the ratio \(1.5\text{ L}:250\text{ mL}\) is greater.
questions.hint: Find the two unit rates before deciding which is greater.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Mass Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two mass ratios by converting kilograms to grams.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(3\text{ kg}:600\text{ g}\) or \(4\text{ kg}:1\text{ kg}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert both ratios to grams. \(3\text{ kg}:600\text{ g}=3{,}000:600=5\). \(4\text{ kg}:1\text{ kg}=4{,}000:1{,}000=4\). Since \(5>4\), the ratio \(3\text{ kg}:600\text{ g}\) is greater.
questions.hint: Convert corresponding quantities to a common unit before comparing.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Length Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two length ratios by converting metres to centimetres.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(2\text{ m}:40\text{ cm}\) or \(5\text{ m}:1.2\text{ m}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert both ratios to centimetres. \(2\text{ m}:40\text{ cm}=200:40=5\). \(5\text{ m}:1.2\text{ m}=500:120=25:6\approx 4.167\). Since \(5>4.167\), the ratio \(2\text{ m}:40\text{ cm}\) is greater.
questions.hint: Express each ratio in the same units and in the same order.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Volume Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two volume ratios by converting litres to millilitres.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(250\text{ mL}:1\text{ L}\) or \(600\text{ mL}:2.5\text{ L}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert litres to millilitres. \(250\text{ mL}:1\text{ L}=250:1{,}000=1:4=0.25\). \(600\text{ mL}:2.5\text{ L}=600:2{,}500=6:25=0.24\). Since \(0.25>0.24\), the ratio \(250\text{ mL}:1\text{ L}\) is greater.
questions.hint: Find the two unit rates before deciding which is greater.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Mass Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two mass ratios by converting kilograms to grams.
questions.question: Which statement is correct for \(1.2\text{ kg}:800\text{ g}\) and \(0.9\text{ kg}:600\text{ g}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert kilograms to grams. \(1.2\text{ kg}:800\text{ g}=1{,}200:800=3:2=1.5\). \(0.9\text{ kg}:600\text{ g}=900:600=3:2=1.5\). Since both ratios simplify to \(3:2\), they are equal.
questions.hint: Convert corresponding quantities to a common unit before comparing.
